text:
zofia: Filing a weird one - onboarding sample intermittently gets duplicate POSTs for small file upload when device is on a corporate VPN. Server sees two identical POSTs ~300ms apart. Not reproducible on Wi-Fi off VPN.

zofia: Details: Retrofit suspend upload, RequestBody streams file as chunked (no Content-Length). Android 11/13 physical devices mostly. OkHttp 4.10 in sample.

marc: Interesting. Does VPN/proxy rewrite or terminate TLS? Chunked uploads + middleboxes sometimes buffer and replay chunks on resume which can look like duplicate requests.

zofia: The VPN is a user-space tunnel (WireGuard-like) on the device. I captured server logs: first connection closes early with RST, client immediately opens a new connection and repeats the request body.

len: That sounds like retry-on-failure behavior. OkHttp can retry idempotent requests, but POSTs are typically not retried unless network failure happens during the send and the client believes body can be retransmitted. With chunked (streaming) bodies OkHttp can't rewind the body unless it's buffered.

marc: Right - streaming bodies are not repeatable by default. OkHttp has logic to replay when connection fails mid-flight for some cases. Also some middleboxes ACK the initial headers but then drop the stream causing client to reopen.

zofia: Repro notes: switch device to VPN, run sample upload (small ~20KB), sometimes backend gets two POSTs, sometimes one. Emulator never reproduces.

len: Quick mitigations: 1) buffer small uploads: `RequestBody.create(mediaType, byteArray)` so OkHttp can resend; 2) set `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` on the client used for uploads; 3) set `callTimeout` to bound how long a hung send can cause retries.

zofia: I tried buffering and disabling retryOnConnectionFailure -> no duplicates in 200 runs. Buffering is a fine onboarding change.

marc: Another approach is to set `Expect: 100-continue` so the client waits for server to accept before sending body, reducing chance of duplicate body sends on mid-write errors. But not all servers/middleboxes honor it well.

len: And if you have to stream (large files) consider multipart chunking with resumable uploads instead of raw streaming in the sample app. For DX, avoid streaming in the default quickstart.

zofia: Also found a subtlety: on some devices HTTP/2 was enabled and the VPN stack handled connection resets differently. Forcing HTTP/1_1 for the client running under the dev flag eliminated a few flakier cases.

docs-bot: Note suggestion: update onboarding guide - recommend buffered bodies for small uploads, show code for `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)`, and add a troubleshooting section "VPN/proxy + streaming uploads" with recommended flags.

zofia: I'll prepare a tiny sample change: buffer by default for files < 128KB, add an opt-in streaming example, and add diagnostic log that prints when `http.proxyHost` or vpn route detected.

ci-bot: CI job created: https://ci.internal/repro/2798765432-upload-vpn-dup-1 (device matrix included).

marc: One more test: add an instrumented test that runs upload under toggled `retryOnConnectionFailure` and asserts server saw no duplicate when buffering is enabled. Good for catching regressions.

zofia: Will add tests + PR to sample + docs update. Filing upstream if we can capture packet trace showing early RST from VPN.
